one_liner: Voice, video, and text communication platform with a broad developer API.
auth_notes: OAuth2 is used for user authentication and bot interactions, while bot tokens (API keys) authenticate bot applications.
access_notes: Sign up for a free developer account on the Discord Developer Portal to create applications and bots at no cost.
api_notes: Comprehensive REST and Gateway WebSocket APIs covering channels, guilds, users, messages, and voice base URL https://discord.com/api/v10
blocker_notes: Public API is fully self-serve and accessible for developers.

auth.quote: This guide explains how to authenticate users with their existing Discord accounts via OAuth2, enabling seamless login and access to Discord features.

access.quote: Previously, apps in fewer than 100 servers could access Privileged Intents by toggling them on in the Developer Portal, and apps in 100+ servers needed to apply for access.

mcp.src: GitHub - jb-bz/jb-discord-mcp: A TypeScript-based MCP server and client for Discord.
mcp.quote: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that enables AI agents to interact with Discord through standardized tools. Built with TypeScript and the official MCP SDK.

verdict.quote: You can turn privileged intents on and off from the Developer Portal as needed. No need to apply for access.

rounds.change_log: Corrected mcp to community_only as there are third-party GitHub community integrations for Discord MCP rather than an official vendor-published server.

reasons.auth: Discord provides a bot token that is used as a static bearer token for API calls (see source 3 and 4).
reasons.access: Bot tokens are obtained for free via the Discord Developer Portal (source 3).
reasons.mcp: MCP servers for Discord are community projects on GitHub (sources 2‑4); no official MCP server is published by Discord.
reasons.verdict: With a free bot token and public REST/WebSocket APIs, a toolkit can be built today.
